subject: Hosting options + residency constraints — next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sven Rasmussen <sven@nordicpay.com>
Cc: Anna Lindqvist <anna@nordicpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, legal@nordicpay.com
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 08:14:00 +0100
Subject: Hosting options + residency constraints — next steps

Hi Sven / Anna —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of what we heard
- NordicPay requires payment-related data and any cardholder-identifying fields to remain within the EU (no cross-border replicas for that subset).
- You’re open to Hosted if the data plane and logs can be constrained to EU-only; otherwise you prefer Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) for tighter controls.
- Primary latency goal is sub-120ms RTT from major Nordic regions to the inference endpoint for real-time fraud scoring.
- Secondary requirement: disaster recovery fallback that can fail over to APAC in extreme scenarios, but only for non-sensitive telemetry (anonymized traces/metrics).

How Redwood maps to those requirements
- Hosted (EU-only): fastest to production; we can offer an EU-only data plane (no US fallbacks) and region-restricted storage for request payloads and logs. Good if you want managed ops and fast time-to-value.
- Dedicated: Reserved GPU pools within an EU region, customer-isolated tenancy, optional bring-your-own-key (BYOK) KMS integration (HSM-backed). Better for predictable throughput and stricter data isolation.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Full control over networking and data residency, support for air-gapped deployments and on-prem inference; longest lead time and higher operational lift but meets the strictest regulatory requirements.

Open questions we need you to confirm
1) Do you require full cardholder data to be prevented from leaving the EU (no backups/replicas outside EU under any circumstance), or is tokenized/anonymized data allowed to replicate?
2) For BYOK: do you need HSM-backed KMS (FIPS level) with customer-managed keys, or is KMS via Redwood with strict EU residency sufficient?
3) For DR: is an APAC fallback acceptable for only anonymized telemetry + model cache warm-up, or must all traffic always remain in-region?

Attachments & artifacts
- Attached: redwood-hosting-summary.pdf (short stub with EU hosting and certs list).
- We’ll share SOC 2 Type II evidence, ISO27001 summary, and our DPA link ahead of the technical workshop.

Proposed next steps
- Technical workshop (90m) with your infra + security, and Redwood’s solutions lead (Karthik) + CSM (Marissa). Suggested slots: Wed 16 Feb 09:00 CET or Thu 17 Feb 14:00 CET.
- We’ll prepare a focused POC plan: two-week smoke test (Hosted EU) vs Dedicated EU capacity sizing; estimated POC timeline 6–8 weeks end-to-end if you choose Dedicated/Private.
- Please send your security questionnaire or a link to the shared folder where we should upload compliance artifacts.

If you want, I can draft a 1-page recommendation (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) after you confirm the answers to the three questions above.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Sven Rasmussen <sven@nordicpay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anna Lindqvist <anna@nordicpay.com>, legal@nordicpay.com
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 11:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Hosting options + residency constraints — next steps

Thanks Ben — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Cardholder data residency: we cannot allow primary cardholder data to leave the EU under any circumstances. That includes backups or replicas. Tokenized or strictly anonymized telemetry is fine to replicate for analytics.

2) BYOK/KMS: we prefer an HSM-backed, customer-controlled KMS (FIPS certification preferred). We need to understand the exact envelope encryption flows Redwood supports for both Dedicated and Private options.

3) DR/fallbacks: APAC fallback is acceptable only for anonymized telemetry and model cache warming — production scoring traffic must be EU-only. 

4) Compliance artifacts: please share SOC 2 Type II report summary and the DPA; our legal team will run the DPA + subprocessor list.

We can do the technical workshop on Wed 16 Feb 09:00 CET. Will invite our infra lead (Anna) and our security SME (legal@).

On a separate note — can you include an initial ballpark of Dedicated capacity pricing for sustained 200 req/s with 512-token average? We’re trying to size internal budget.

Regards,
Sven
Head of Infrastructure — NordicPay

Looping in a short technical checklist so we’re ready for Wed’s workshop. I’ll lead the tech portion and bring a sample Dedicated EU config + BYOK flow.

Technical prep (what I need from NordicPay before the workshop)
- Exact list of data elements that must remain in the EU (field-level). If you have a sample payload (redacted) that’s ideal.
- Network connectivity: do you prefer VPC peering or private link? Any ILB/FW requirements?
- KMS/HSM details: vendor, required certs (FIPS), and whether you need on-prem HSM vs cloud-HSM in your VPC.
- Throughput profile: 200 req/s sustained, but confirm peak bursts and average token length distribution.

What I’ll present in the workshop
- Concrete Hosted EU dataflow diagram showing where logs, caches, and KV stores live and how we enforce EU residency.
- Dedicated EU topology with optional BYOK HSM integration and encryption-in-transit + at-rest flows.
- POC plan: smoke test (Hosted EU) vs Dedicated sizing trial; expected data collection and success criteria.

One note on cross-region fallback: we can design a policy that only allows anonymized telemetry/metrics to cross into APAC for DR, while production scoring endpoints have an explicit deny for non-EU egress. I’ll include that policy sample.

I’ve attached a minimal Dedicated EU config stub for reference. I’ll also prepare a short pricing worksheet to convert model choices into a committed capacity estimate for the quote.

Thanks — see you on Wed.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
